text: Some people focus on conversion rate, like, "I'm going to make this really, really slick." And that's cool. You get a bit more growth. But to get to recommendation, you're going to blow your user socks off.
speaker: Nilan Peiris
context: Lenny is discussing with Nilan how to drive word-of-mouth growth for products. Nilan is explaining that most teams stop when their product simply works, or they focus on incremental improvements like conversion rate optimization. However, to get customers to actively recommend your product to others, you need to exceed their expectations dramatically. He argues that you must create experiences that customers never knew were possible before - essentially doing something completely new rather than just improving existing solutions.
text_ko: 어떤 사람들은 전환율(conversion rate)에만 집중해요. "정말정말 세련되게 만들 거야" 이렇게요. 그건 좋아요 — 성장도 좀 더 나와요. 그런데 진짜 추천(recommendation)을 얻으려면 사용자들을 완전히 놀라게 해서 강한 인상을 남겨야 해요.
text_zh: 有些人只盯着转化率（conversion rate），想着“我要把这做得特别顺滑、特别有质感。”这确实能带来点增长，但要做到用户愿意主动推荐你，你得把他们彻底惊艳。
text_es: Algunas personas se centran en la tasa de conversión (conversion rate), tipo: "voy a dejar esto súper, súper pulido". Y eso está bien — consigues un poco más de crecimiento. Pero para llegar a la recomendación (recommendation), tienes que dejar boquiabiertos a tus usuarios.
key_sentence: To get recommendations, you must blow your user socks off with unique experiences.
original_text: Some people focus on conversion rate, like, "I'm going to make this really, really slick." And that's cool. You get a bit more growth. But to get to recommendation, you're going to blow your user socks off. You have to give them an experience they didn't know was previously possible. And when you are in that place of doing something that no one has ever done before, that's when you get it.

vocabulary.definition: The percentage of users who take a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up for a newsletter, out of the total number of visitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, conversion rate is a critical metric used to evaluate the effectiveness of marketing strategies and user experience design.
vocabulary.nuance: While a high conversion rate indicates successful user engagement, it is important to also consider the quality of the conversions and customer satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: A suggestion or endorsement made by an individual or organization, often based on personal experience or expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, recommendations can significantly influence consumer behavior, often driving sales and fostering brand loyalty through trust and credibility.
vocabulary.nuance: Recommendations carry weight when they stem from genuine experiences, making them more impactful than mere advertisements.

text: So building a brand led money transfer business, the brand's got to be pretty damn good, right? You're going to feel pretty special afterwards, in order to have less money afterwards.
speaker: Nilan Peiris
context: Lenny asks about the biggest shift that helped Wise grow word-of-mouth significantly. Nilan explains why word-of-mouth was essential for Wise's business model. Since money is the ultimate commodity and customers end up with less money after using any money transfer service, building a brand-led business in this space requires an exceptionally good customer experience. He's outlining the challenge of finding marketing channels that can scale broadly while having very low distribution costs, which led them to focus on word-of-mouth growth.
text_ko: 브랜드 주도형 송금 사업(brand-led money transfer business)을 만들려면 브랜드가 정말 끝내줘야 해요, 그렇죠? 결국엔 돈은 덜 남는데도 ‘그래도 기분은 특별하잖아’ 하면서 스스로 위로하게 될 거예요.
text_zh: 所以想把汇款业务做成以品牌为主导(brand-led money transfer business)，品牌得足够出色，对吧？最后你会觉得自己很了不起，但手里的钱反而更少了。
text_es: Si vas a montar un negocio de transferencias de dinero centrado en la marca (brand-led money transfer business), la marca tiene que ser realmente buena, ¿no? Te vas a sentir muy especial… para luego quedarte con menos dinero.
key_sentence: the brand's got to be pretty damn good, right?
original_text: So building a brand led money transfer business, the brand's got to be pretty damn good, right? You're going to feel pretty special afterwards, in order to have less money afterwards. So what we're looking for always, but what channels out there are super scalable, and can reach our entire audience, but have an incredibly low distribution cost.

vocabulary.definition: A brand is a unique name, symbol, or design that identifies and differentiates a product or service from others in the market. It encompasses the perceptions and experiences associated with a company or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a strong brand can lead to customer loyalty, higher perceived value, and competitive advantage, making it a crucial element for startups and established companies alike.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'brand' often refers to the visual identity, it also implies the emotional connection and reputation a company builds over time.

vocabulary.definition: Money transfer refers to the process of sending funds from one individual or entity to another, often facilitated by financial institutions or digital platforms. It can occur domestically or internationally.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the fintech sector, money transfer services are critical for enabling seamless transactions, especially in global markets where traditional banking may be less accessible.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply various methods, including electronic transfers, wire transfers, or remittances, and is often associated with speed and security.

text: We only got the advocacy when we were eight to 10 times cheaper. That's when people started talking about it. So the bar is all the way up there. And to put that in context, that means figuring out how to move money instantly.
speaker: Nilan Peiris
context: Nilan is explaining a key insight about driving word-of-mouth for Wise. When entering new markets, they discovered that being marginally better (like pricing at 5.9% versus competitors at 6%) would get customers to use their service, but wouldn't generate recommendations. Only when they achieved dramatically better pricing - 8 to 10 times cheaper than alternatives - did customers become evangelical and start talking about the product. This taught them that the bar for recommendation is extremely high, requiring breakthrough improvements rather than incremental ones.
text_ko: 사람들이 얘기하기 시작한 건 우리가 8~10배나 더 싸졌을 때뿐이에요. 그때야 고객 추천(advocacy)이 나왔죠. 그래서 기준이 아주 높아진 거예요. 맥락을 더하면, 결국 돈을 즉시 이체하는 방법(즉시 자금 이체, move money instantly)을 찾아내야 한다는 뜻이에요.
text_zh: 只有当我们的价格便宜到8到10倍，才会有人开始主动推荐(advocacy)。那时候大家才开始讨论它。所以门槛被拉得很高。换句话说，这就得想明白怎么做到资金即时到账(move money instantly)。
text_es: Solo conseguimos apoyo (advocacy) cuando éramos entre ocho y diez veces más baratos. Fue entonces cuando empezó a correr la voz. Así que el listón está por las nubes. Y para que te hagas una idea, eso significa averiguar cómo mover dinero al instante.
key_sentence: Advocacy only emerged when we were all the way down to 0.35.
original_text: We only got the advocacy when we were eight to 10 times cheaper. That's when people started talking about it. So the bar is all the way up there. And to put that in context, that means figuring out how to move money instantly. That means figuring out how to drop the price all the way from six all the way down to 0.35.

vocabulary.definition: Advocacy refers to the act of supporting or promoting a cause or proposal, often through persuasive communication and action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, advocacy can involve lobbying for policy changes, promoting a product, or rallying support from stakeholders to influence decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While advocacy is generally positive, it can sometimes carry a connotation of bias or partisanship, so it's important to ensure that the support is based on sound reasoning and evidence.

vocabulary.definition: Context refers to the circumstances or background information surrounding a particular event, situation, or concept that helps to clarify its meaning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, providing context is crucial for understanding market trends, customer behavior, or the rationale behind strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a broader perspective, so it's important to use it when the surrounding details significantly affect interpretation or understanding.

text: It's this thing around growth rate. So, especially product net growth, which is what we're talking about. So you can imagine, we're going to open a new market to Indonesia, and the fastest way to do it is to take...
speaker: Nilan Peiris
context: Lenny asks about common mistakes people make when trying to drive word-of-mouth growth. Nilan explains a key misstep that many companies, including Wise, have made. When entering new markets, the tempting shortcut is to use existing infrastructure solutions that others have already built - for example, plugging into existing money transfer systems for Indonesia. While this approach can quickly acquire some users, it doesn't create the exponential growth curve needed for strong word-of-mouth because it hasn't fundamentally solved the underlying problems customers face.
text_ko: 이건 성장률에 관한 얘기예요. 특히 지금 말하는 건 제품 순성장(product net growth)이구요. 인도네시아처럼 새 시장에 진출한다고 상상해보세요. 그럴 때 가장 빠른 방법은 ... 하는 거예요.
text_zh: 关键在于增长率这事儿。尤其是产品净增长（product net growth），也就是我们在说的那个。你可以想象，我们要进军印尼这个新市场，最快的办法就是...
text_es: Es toda esta cuestión de la tasa de crecimiento. Sobre todo del crecimiento neto del producto (product net growth), que es de lo que estamos hablando. Así que imagínate: vamos a abrir un nuevo mercado en Indonesia, y la forma más rápida de hacerlo es...
key_sentence: the fastest way to do it is to take...
original_text: It's this thing around growth rate. So, especially product net growth, which is what we're talking about. So you can imagine, we're going to open a new market to Indonesia, and the fastest way to do it is to take... Someone else has figured out how to move to Indonesia. We take that infrastructure, and we'll plug it into Wise, you know what? We can do this, we'll get some users. But it doesn't grow like a hockey stick.

vocabulary.definition: The percentage increase in a company's revenue, customer base, or market share over a specific period of time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the growth rate is a critical metric used to assess the performance and potential of a company, especially in evaluating investment opportunities and market strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While a high growth rate is generally viewed positively, it is important to consider the sustainability of that growth and the context in which it occurs.

vocabulary.definition: The overall increase in a company's size or value after accounting for losses or reductions, such as customer churn or product returns.
vocabulary.businessContext: Net growth is often used to provide a more accurate picture of a company's performance, as it reflects the actual gain after subtracting any losses.
vocabulary.nuance: Net growth can sometimes mask underlying issues if not analyzed alongside gross growth figures, making it essential to consider both metrics.

vocabulary.definition: The process of introducing a product or service to a new geographical area or demographic segment where it has not previously been available.
vocabulary.businessContext: Opening a new market is a strategic move for businesses seeking to expand their customer base and increase revenue, often requiring market research and tailored marketing strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies not just entry into a new market but also the establishment of a presence and the cultivation of customer relationships in that area.

text: So it comes from a very logical place, how do I get users quickly? I can take a shortcut in doing this, but that, you kind of realize is wasted effort. So the step then becomes this much harder question of these types of questions.
speaker: Nilan Peiris
context: Continuing his explanation about avoiding shortcuts in product development, Nilan describes how teams naturally want to find quick wins to acquire users rapidly. However, he learned that these shortcuts ultimately represent wasted effort because they don't create the transformative experiences needed for word-of-mouth growth. Instead, teams should ask fundamental questions about the theoretical limits of what's possible - like the absolute minimum cost or maximum speed achievable - and work backwards from those ideals rather than making incremental improvements.
text_ko: 그래서 출발점은 아주 논리적이에요. ‘어떻게 하면 빠르게 사용자를 확보할까?’라고 생각하죠. 이걸 위해 지름길(shortcut)을 택할 수도 있는데, 그러다 보면 그게 결국엔 헛수고라는 걸 깨닫게 돼요. 그래서 그다음엔 훨씬 더 어렵고 복잡한, 이런 종류의 질문들을 고민해야 해요.
text_zh: 这出发点很合理：怎么能快速获取用户(users)？可以走捷径，但你会意识到那是在浪费力气。于是下一步反而成了一个更难的问题——像这种问题该怎么解决？
text_es: Surge de algo muy lógico: ¿cómo consigo usuarios rápido? Podría tomar un atajo para lograrlo, pero te das cuenta de que al final es un esfuerzo desperdiciado. Entonces lo que viene es una pregunta mucho más difícil de ese tipo.
key_sentence: but that, you kind of realize is wasted effort.
original_text: So it comes from a very logical place, how do I get users quickly? I can take a shortcut in doing this, but that, you kind of realize is wasted effort. So the step then becomes this much harder question of these types of questions. Like what is the theoretical minimum cost for moving money into a market? What is the theoretical maximum speed?

vocabulary.definition: A quicker or more direct route to achieve a goal or complete a task, often bypassing standard procedures.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, taking a shortcut may refer to using less rigorous methods to achieve results faster, which can sometimes compromise quality or thoroughness.
vocabulary.nuance: While shortcuts can save time, they may lead to incomplete solutions or future complications, so they should be used judiciously.

vocabulary.definition: Exertion or resources spent on a task that yields little to no productive outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, wasted effort often refers to time and resources that could have been better allocated to more impactful projects or strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase carries a negative connotation, suggesting inefficiency and lack of foresight in planning or execution.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by clear, sound reasoning or consistent principles that lead to rational conclusions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business realm, logical thinking is crucial for decision-making, problem-solving, and strategic planning, ensuring that actions are based on evidence and rationality.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'logical' suggests a rational approach, it may sometimes imply a lack of creativity or emotional consideration in decision-making.

text: You can't split test your way to love. So, this experiment led product management approach, where you throw a bunch of things on the wall, and then you kind of see what sticks, and generally we don't advocate this.
speaker: Nilan Peiris
context: Lenny and Nilan are discussing Wise's approach to product development and experimentation. Nilan is explaining why Wise doesn't rely heavily on A/B testing and experiment-driven product management. He argues that constantly running experiments to see what works is ineffective for building products that customers will love and recommend. Instead of this "throw things at the wall" approach, he advocates for building conviction about what matters to customers through direct customer feedback and insights before building features, since engineering resources are expensive and limited.
text_ko: 사용자의 사랑을 스플릿 테스트(split test)로 얻을 수는 없어요. 그래서 여러 가지를 벽에 막 던져보고 뭐가 붙는지 보는, 이른바 실험 주도형 제품 관리 접근법(experiment led product management approach)은 보통 우리가 권하지 않아요.
text_zh: 靠 A/B 测试(split test) 是让用户真正喜欢起来的办法。 所以那种以实验为主导的产品管理方法(experiment-led product management approach)，就是把很多点子都试一遍，看看哪个能站得住脚——我们一般不建议这么干。
text_es: No vas a lograr que los usuarios lo amen solo con pruebas A/B (split tests). Por eso, ese enfoque de gestión de producto (product management) dirigido por experimentos —en el que lanzas un montón de cosas a ver cuál pega— no es algo que, en general, recomendemos.
key_sentence: You can't split test your way to love.
original_text: You can't split test your way to love. So, this experiment led product management approach, where you throw a bunch of things on the wall, and then you kind of see what sticks, and generally we don't advocate this. Obviously there's a bit of it that happens, but generally don't advocate it. Mainly because engineering is expensive, and you can actually figure out what matters to customers through other means.

vocabulary.definition: The process of overseeing the development, marketing, and lifecycle of a product from conception to market launch and beyond.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product management involves coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure that products meet customer needs and align with business goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While product management focuses on strategic planning and execution, it is often seen as a collaborative role that requires balancing various stakeholder interests.

vocabulary.definition: To publicly support or recommend a particular cause, policy, or idea.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, advocating for a product or strategy often involves rallying support from stakeholders and influencing decision-making processes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'advocate' implies strong support, it can also suggest a level of persuasion that may not always be welcomed, especially in contentious discussions.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; a method or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term 'approach' is often used to describe the strategy taken to achieve goals, whether in project management, marketing, or product development.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply flexibility and adaptability, but may also suggest a lack of specificity if not defined clearly.

text: And closing this delta between what you've done, and what's perceived to be done is what I call product marketing within the product. And that in its own right is a discipline, I've learned.
speaker: Nilan Peiris
context: Nilan is sharing insights about a breakthrough that 3x'd their referral sharing rates. He discovered that customers were getting great value from Wise but weren't fully aware of how much value they were receiving. For example, customers saved money but didn't believe the actual savings amount, or received instant transfers without realizing they were instant. The key was creating visual comparisons and animations within the product to help customers understand the true value they received, which then made them more likely to share with others.
text_ko: 여러분이 실제로 해놓은 것과 사람들이 해놓은 것으로 인식하는 것 사이의 격차를 줄이는 것이 제가 말하는 제품 안에서의 프로덕트 마케팅(product marketing within the product)이에요. 그리고 그게 그 자체로 하나의 전문 분야라는 걸 배웠어요.
text_zh: 要缩小你实际做的事情和别人认为你做的事情之间的差距，我把这叫做产品内的产品营销(product marketing within the product)。我发现这本身就是一门学问。
text_es: Y cerrar esa brecha entre lo que realmente has hecho y lo que se percibe que has hecho es lo que yo llamo marketing del producto dentro del producto. Y eso por sí solo es toda una disciplina, he aprendido.
key_sentence: Closing this delta between actions and perceptions is product marketing in its own right.

vocabulary.definition: Regarded or understood in a particular way, often based on subjective interpretation rather than objective reality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and branding, 'perceived' is crucial as it influences customer attitudes and behaviors toward products or services.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a connotation of subjectivity, suggesting that perceptions may not always align with facts, making it important to clarify the distinction in discussions.

vocabulary.definition: A field of study or a branch of knowledge, often characterized by a systematic approach to learning and practice.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'discipline' refers to the structured methodologies and practices that guide teams in achieving goals, such as product marketing or project management.
vocabulary.nuance: While it can refer to a specific area of expertise, it also implies a level of rigor and commitment to standards, making it suitable for discussions about professional development.
